analysis:
Both supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines ~429-612 and 613 onward). They contain only release-note prose. No executable code, configuration, authorization logic, or schema changes are visible, so no concrete security regression can be established from this text.

The changelog describes security-relevant behavior implemented elsewhere in the PR or in earlier commits, none of which was supplied: App Attest dead-key rotation limits, `EIGENINFERENCE_APP_ATTEST_KEY_ROTATION_PERCENT`, the 6-hour invalidKey backoff, untrusted ready-reply diagnostics (`launch_session`, `boot_time`, `operation_stalled_seconds`), APNs code-identity retries, durable build qualification, per-account first-content SLA, public model-demand aggregates with suppression thresholds, and `darkbloom switch` live model switching.

The prose is consistent with the existing threat model. The App Attest diagnostics are described as untrusted metadata that does not affect authorization, matching TB-002. Rotation is described as never revoking or denying serving, and a fresh attestation must still pass the full checks, matching TB-011. The 0.9.10 text notes that publication of the signed provider is separate from the source version bump, so the changelog does not claim a rollout.

Items the next review pass should check in the actual source, which I did not see:
- Public model-demand history: the stated suppression of cohorts with fewer than 20 requests or 3 accounts, and the exclusion of suppressed cohorts from every resolution so subtraction cannot recover hidden counts. This is a possible privacy surface related to T-058/T-051.
- App Attest rotation admission and machine-merge serialization: the claim that rotation never bypasses the budget and never grants authorization (TB-011, T-053, T-055, T-057).
- Unauthenticated `ready` diagnostics: bounds on size, parsing and logging (TB-002).
- Rotated keys: that they cannot inherit an old authorization or lease.
- `darkbloom report` under sudo: it reads the invoking user's credentials and config files (token and state file). Check the privilege and upload boundaries and redaction.
- `darkbloom switch`: confirm the new model selection cannot bypass coordinator model-hash and capability gating.

There is a coverage limit: no code was provided, so this is not evidence that the described behavior is safe. needs_deeper_review is true only because the documented behavior touches security-relevant code that was not visible.
